facts.title: Bowing Is a Complex and Essential Part of Japanese Etiquette
facts.summary: Bowing, or ojigi, is a central part of Japanese etiquette, and how deeply and how long a person bows signals how much respect they are showing.

facts.title: Cherry Blossoms Symbolize the Fleeting Nature of Life in Japan
facts.summary: In Japan, cherry blossoms are a symbol of life's brevity: the flowers burst open, then fall within days.

facts.title: Godzilla Was Created as a Metaphor for Nuclear Weapons
facts.summary: Godzilla, who first appeared in Toho's 1954 film Godzilla, was conceived as a metaphor for nuclear weapons.

facts.title: Japan Has About 25,000 Natural Hot Spring Sources
facts.summary: Japan has approximately 25,000 hot spring sources, and about 3,000 onsen establishments use naturally hot spring water.

facts.title: Japan Feels More Than 2,000 Earthquakes a Year
facts.summary: People in Japan feel more than 2,000 earthquakes in a typical year, and instruments detect far more.

facts.title: Japan Has 14,125 Islands, More Than Double the Count Long Cited
facts.summary: Japan is made up of 14,125 islands, according to a recount published by the Geospatial Information Authority of Japan in 2023.

facts.title: Japan Has Seen Over 300 Unique Kit Kat Flavors
facts.summary: Nestlé has released more than 300 limited-edition Kit Kat flavors in Japan since the early 2000s, many of them seasonal or sold only in particular regions.

facts.title: Japanese Convenience Stores Offer Fresh Meals and Everyday Services
facts.summary: Japan's convenience stores, known as konbini, sell fresh food but also work as small service centres for everyday errands.

facts.title: Karaoke Was Invented in Japan Around 1970
facts.summary: Karaoke was born in Japan around the turn of the 1970s, and its name combines kara, meaning 'empty', with a shortened form of ōkesutora, 'orchestra'.

facts.title: Kendo Is a Modern Japanese Martial Art Based on Samurai Swordsmanship
facts.summary: Kendo, meaning 'the way of the sword', is a modern Japanese martial art descended from kenjutsu, the swordsmanship of the samurai.

facts.title: The Summit of Mount Fuji Belongs to a Shinto Shrine
facts.summary: The top of Mount Fuji, Japan's highest peak, is the property of a Shinto shrine.

facts.title: The 'Lucky Cat' Figurine Is Japanese, and It Is Beckoning, Not Waving
facts.summary: The popular lucky cat figurine is the Japanese maneki-neko, whose name means 'beckoning cat', and its raised paw is beckoning rather than waving.

facts.title: Tipping Is Not Customary in Japan and Can Come Across as Rude
facts.summary: Tipping is not customary in Japan, and in many situations offering extra money can be considered rude or even insulting.

facts.title: Tokyo's Robot Restaurant Turned Dinner Into a Neon Robot Show
facts.summary: Tokyo's Robot Restaurant, in the Kabukichō nightlife district of Shinjuku, served dinner alongside a loud, neon-lit stage show starring robots and dancers.

facts.title: Tokyo Once Hosted the World's Largest Fish Market
facts.summary: Until 2018, Tokyo's Tsukiji market was the largest wholesale fish and seafood market in the world.

facts.title: Many Yakuza Members Have Elaborate Full-Body Tattoos
facts.summary: Many yakuza members wear elaborate full-body tattoos in the traditional Japanese style known as irezumi.
